core.title: Give every exposed frontend journey a responsive browser spec
core.given: A journey whose entrypoint is exposed and whose surfaces include frontend (or declare none) exists in the plan
core.when: the journey set is declared, changed or evaluated (including plan-only changes and already-declared journeys)
core.then: That journey MUST have a browser spec (recognized as defined in verification) bound to it by the stack's journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) and carrying the stack's responsive test URN (profile: urn.test_kinds#responsive_test).
prefer: Add a responsive browser spec for the journey, placed per the stack's e2e location (profile: layout.e2e_location) and bound with the stack's journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey).
Add the responsive browser spec as soon as the plan declares a new exposed frontend journey.
avoid: Counting a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string as responsive coverage.

Assuming a misnamed spec escapes judgement: any test file whose header comments carry a journey recognition marker (profile: urn.header#journey_markers) is judged as a browser spec, even when its name does not match the stack's e2e test kind (profile: suffix.e2e_test).
Writing responsive browser specs for internal journeys or journeys whose surfaces exclude frontend just to raise coverage.
unless: The journey is internal, or its exposed entrypoint surfaces exclude frontend — there is no screen to fit, so it is out of scope.
Vendored and generated trees (the stack's excluded trees, profile: roots.excluded) are never scanned.
core.why: Every screen a user can reach should be proven to fit from mobile to desktop; exposed journeys are exactly those screens, and new ones appear here as soon as the plan declares them.
evidence: For each exposed journey with surfaces including frontend (or none declared), a browser spec exists whose header carries the stack's journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) and the stack's responsive test URN (profile: urn.test_kinds#responsive_test).
The stack's convention check for this rule reports no uncovered exposed journey.
verification: A browser spec is recognized as: a file of the stack's e2e test kind (profile: suffix.e2e_test) run by the stack's test runner (profile: tooling.test_runner), OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey recognition marker from the stack's full marker set (profile: urn.header#journey_markers), so a misnamed one is still judged.

Recognition and qualifying coverage are distinct: recognition markers (profile: urn.header#journey_markers) only classify a file as a browser spec; qualifying coverage additionally requires the spec's header to carry the stack's journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) and the stack's responsive test URN (profile: urn.test_kinds#responsive_test), independently of which branch recognized the file as a browser spec. A file recognized only through an alternative recognition marker does not by itself satisfy coverage.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser spec.

Scope: journeys with an exposed entrypoint whose surfaces include frontend or declare no surfaces; skip internal journeys and those whose surfaces exclude frontend. Evaluate every in-scope journey, not only those touched by the change; a journey is covered if any qualifying bound responsive spec remains.
Never scan the stack's vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded).

Path hints (the e2e file kind and the e2e root, profiles: suffix.e2e_test, roots.e2e) are non-exhaustive: matching a path is observable, but plan/journey declarations and misnamed marker-bearing test files can have arbitrary names, so globs neither define scope nor exhaustively locate inputs.

Activation and checking need a semantic plan/journey observer that reads each journey's entrypoint exposure and surfaces wherever the declaration lives (not by filename), plus a spec-binding observer that maps journey bindings (profile: urn.binding.journey), recognition markers (profile: urn.header#journey_markers) and responsive test URNs (profile: urn.test_kinds#responsive_test) in test-file headers across all test files. The rule fires for plan-only changes and for pre-existing uncovered journeys, not only when specs are edited, and the check evaluates all in-scope journeys against all remaining qualifying specs.

values: journey declared, changed or evaluated in the plan with an exposed entrypoint
journey entrypoint exposure or surfaces changed
responsive browser spec or journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) added/removed/renamed
exposed frontend journey without a bound responsive browser spec
files of the stack's e2e test kind (profile: suffix.e2e_test)
files under the stack's e2e root (profile: roots.e2e)

fires: The plan (even in a plan-only change) declares a journey with an exposed entrypoint and surfaces including frontend, and no test file anywhere carries the stack's journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) together with the stack's responsive test URN (profile: urn.test_kinds#responsive_test) for it.
An existing exposed journey that declares no surfaces has no bound responsive browser spec, even though no spec was edited in this change.
A responsive spec for an exposed frontend journey is deleted or its journey binding (profile: urn.binding.journey) is removed, and no other qualifying responsive spec remains bound to that journey.

For an exposed frontend journey, the only bound responsive spec is a misnamed test file (not of the stack's e2e test kind, profile: suffix.e2e_test) whose header comments carry a journey recognition marker (profile: urn.header#journey_markers); it is judged as a browser spec and counts (or fails) as that journey's coverage.
doesNotFire: An exposed journey whose entrypoint surfaces exclude frontend.
Files under the stack's excluded (vendored and generated) trees (profile: roots.excluded).
A responsive spec is deleted but another qualifying responsive browser spec remains bound to the same journey.
A test file is recognised as a browser spec but is not bound to any in-scope (exposed, frontend-surfaced) journey; spec classification alone is not this rule's scope.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file-name patterns that identify the stack's e2e (browser) spec files, which count as browser specs by kind.
The stack's test runner; for this rule, the runner that executes the e2e browser specs — a file of the stack's e2e test kind run by it is a browser spec.

The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a journey; in Bun it is a header comment, and together with the responsive test URN it must sit in the spec's header to qualify as that journey's coverage.

The stack's full set of header-comment journey markers by which any test file is recognized (judged) as a browser spec, including misnamed files; a superset of urn.binding.journey used for recognition only — an alternative marker alone does not provide the binding required for coverage.

neutralityNotes: RESP is ATDD-Bun's abbreviation for a responsive browser spec; the core spells it out ('responsive browser spec' / 'responsive test URN'), which changes no obligation. Plan-model terms (journey, exposed entrypoint, surfaces including frontend, internal journey) are treated as stack-neutral ATDD plan semantics: bun.json itself says the journey declaration is read wherever it lives, not by filename, so no profile key is needed for journey declaration and the required plan/journey and spec-binding observers are declared needs_new_observer and described in core verification. Header placement is preserved exactly: bun.json evidence[0] requires the journey binding and the RESP test URN in the browser spec's header, so core evidence[0] and the qualifying-coverage verification entry require both in the spec's header independently of which branch recognized the file as a browser spec ('header' is a stack-neutral file concept, and bun.json's then, like the core's, does not itself say 'header'). The unit-test anti-pattern keeps bun.json's generic wording — a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not coverage — not narrowed to the responsive test URN. Browser-spec recognition and qualifying coverage remain deliberately separate: recognition uses the stack's full journey marker set (urn.header#journey_markers, all four Bun alternatives preserved), while coverage requires the journey binding (urn.binding.journey, only // Journey: <journey id>) plus a responsive test URN (urn.test_kinds#responsive_test) whose shape bun.json does not pin, so no shape is asserted. The e2e runner is taken from the existing tooling.test_runner key rather than a new one. Detector/validator/finding ids (htmx_e2e_detector) and the audit alias stay with the Bun realization (bunOnly). 'Misnamed' (avoid[1], fires[3]) means a test file not matching the stack's e2e test kind, expressed via profile suffix.e2e_test. Two keys were missing from the closed vocabulary (journey recognition markers; the responsive test URN) and are proposed in the urn group.
